title: רב יוסף

paragraphs: (1) The unqualified Rav Yosef is bar Chiyya: Chullin 18b; end of Radbaz’s principles. His teacher was Rav Yehudah; his colleague, Rabbah bar Nachmani. Rava was his student.

(2) He was blind. Mekor Chayim, end of Shelach Lekha, writes: ‘They said that Rav Yosef sat in a dark house for forty days, ordered marble stones brought before him, looked at them, and became blind. This is undoubtedly the utmost abstinence. They said Rav Ashi did likewise. One of the great physicians became blind; physicians came to heal him, but he said: I do not wish to see any more, for what I have seen suffices. The Greek sage spoke well: not seeing certain things is better than seeing them.’ End quotation. HaChovel 87a: he said, ‘At first I used to say: Whoever tells me a blind person is exempt from the commandments, I shall make a feast for the rabbis,’ and so forth, ‘because I am exempt yet perform them. Now that they have said,’ and so forth, ‘one who is commanded is greater,’ and so forth.

(3) He was versed in Targum; therefore they said ‘as Rav Yosef translates.’ See Tosafot, Bava Kamma 3b. Shalshelet HaKabbalah writes Bava Kamma, chapter 3; this is a scribal error. Since one may not recite the Written Torah orally, and he was blind, he said it in translation. Ritva, Megillah, chapter 1, 3, likewise writes this. Berakhot 28a: nogei mi-moed. Shabbat 64a, end: ‘This is what we translate: machokh.’ Pesachim 68a: ‘And the ruins of the fat ones,’ and the wicked’s property. Yoma 32b, end, and 77b, end; Moed Katan 26a and 28b; Kiddushin 13a: ‘And they broke out in adultery.’ There, 72b: On ‘A mamzer shall dwell in Ashdod,’ Rav Yosef gave a Targum. Nedarim 38a; Nazir 3a—ס״א [provisionally another text] does not have it; see Orach Mishor. Chelek 94b: Rav Yosef said, ‘Were it not for this verse’s translation.’ ‘As Rav Yosef translates’: Avodah Zarah 44a and Menachot 110a. He was versed in mishnayot; he and Rav Sheshet both habitually repeated mishnayot. Since they were blind and repeated orally, and one may not say written matters orally, they repeated mishnayot (Berit Shalom, Mikketz).

(4) He became ill and forgot his learning: Nedarim 41a. He said: ‘Master of Abraham! He hangs what is taught upon what is not taught’: Ketubbot 2a and Makkot 4a. Eruvin 41a, 66b, beginning, 73a, 89b: Rav Yosef said, ‘I did not hear this matter.’ Chapter 1, 10a, Rashi explains: I did not hear Rabbah son of Rav Huna’s statement from his father Rav Huna. There, 75b, Rav Bivi told him: ‘I said it in Rav Adda bar Ahavah’s name.’ Rav Yosef said: ‘Master of Abraham! “Many” became confused for me with “Rabbi.” I am Rav Yehudah’s student and did not hear it from him.’ Abaye told him: ‘You said it.’ Rashi explains in all the places above that he became ill and forgot his learning. Pesachim 13a, end: Rav Adda bar Mattanah told him, ‘You told us explicitly.’ Rashi explains: he forgot his learning when ill, and his students reminded him. Therefore Rav Yosef said in Menachot 99a [printed: Zevachim corrected to Menachot 59a]—‘Beware concerning an elder who has forgotten his learning,’ because he saw that they were not treating him respectfully.

(5) When Abaye objected, he told him: ‘בזויים חד ברא הוי לכייליל ולא מתקן’—provisionally, ‘Disgraceful! Kaylil had one son, and he is still uncorrected’: Zevachim 118b. When he answered on his behalf he said of him: ‘The master, being a great man, knows what I mean.’ He called those objecting ‘sons of Keturah,’ there, 62a, end. When Rabbi Zeira went up, he ate meat from an animal slaughtered outside the area permitted by Rav and Shmuel; see his entry. They asked him: ‘Are you not from Rav and Shmuel’s place?’ He replied: ‘Who said it? Rav Yosef bar Chiyya, who learns from everyone.’ Rav Yosef heard and was angry: ‘I learned from Rav Yehudah, who used to repeat even teachings of uncertain attribution’; see his entry. At the end of Eglah Arufah he said: ‘Do not teach that humility ceased, for I am here.’ He split wood in honor of the Sabbath: Kol Kitvei 119a. Yalkut Reuveni, Yitro 102b, end, in Peliah’s name: see blind Rav Yosef, who, when he heard his mother coming, said, ‘I shall rise before the Divine Presence.’ Rabbi—it should read Rav—Yosef had a corner of a vineyard which he hoed with an extra hoeing; it produced wine which took twice the usual amount of water: Menachot 87a. He said: ‘Three people’s lives are not lives: the compassionate, the irascible, and the fastidious. All are in me’: Arvei Pesachim 113b. Sukkah 29a and Bava Batra 23a: ‘I am fastidious.’ He fasted 120 fasts, meaning three periods of forty days. Our reading ‘another hundred’ is a scribal error and should read forty, Maharshal. Finally they recited to him, ‘They shall not depart from your mouth, nor your seed’s mouth,’ and so forth: Bava Metzia 85a, end.

(6) Rabbah and Rav Yosef were in Pumbedita after Rav Yehudah, as related in Gittin, HaNizakin; see his entry. The shofar that was in Rav Yehudah’s house was afterwards in Rabbah’s, and afterwards in Rav Yosef’s; see Naarah. He exchanged his meal on Purim and during mourning with Rabbah; see his entry. Rav Yosef knew the Account of the Chariot, and Pumbedita’s elders the Account of Creation; they asked one another to teach them: Chagigah 13a. Rava said: ‘The Pumbeditans know,’ meaning Rav Yosef, HaMaksheh 72a. Hini and Shili were near Pumbedita, where Rabbah and Rav Yosef sat: Rashi, Bava Metzia 63b. צ״ד [provisionally Tzemach David] writes that Rav Yosef sat on Rabbah’s throne at Sura—this is incorrect; it was Pumbedita—in 4082 and died in 4085. So too Yuchasin, sequence of transmission from Yesod Olam. Rav Sherira Gaon’s epistle there says he died in 634 of the contracts era, which is 4082. Each told the other, ‘You preside,’ and did not accept: end of Berakhot 64 and Horayot 14. They sent from there: Rav Yosef was Sinai—Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said, ‘Sinai said’; Rashi explains Rav Yosef, Moed Katan 12a and Eruvin 30a, because he was versed in mishnayot—while Rabbah uprooted mountains. Which was preferable? They said: everyone needs the master of wheat. Nevertheless Rav Yosef did not accept, because the Chaldeans said he would preside two and a half years. Rabbah presided twenty-two years. All the time Rabbah presided, he did not even summon a bloodletter to his house; see Rashi at Horayot’s end. Rav Hai Gaon explains differently; Ramah explains that he was not ill; see ב״ש [provisionally Beer Sheva]. The matter of the prepared hide, whether a change of name is like a physical change: Rabbah pressed Rav Yosef for twenty-two years without resolution, until Rav Yosef presided and resolved that it was like a physical change: Merubbah 66b. Ketubbot 42b: Rava said, ‘This matter of the fine was difficult,’ and so forth, until Rav Yosef presided. For the ruling against Rabbah, see his entry. He applied to himself ‘Much produce comes through an ox’s strength.’ Tosafot say this is because Yosef is called an ox: Sanhedrin 42a. It appears the verse hints at Joseph in Egypt, ‘His firstborn ox,’ who gathered much produce; Bereshit Rabbah, Vayishlach, end of section 75: the ox is Joseph. Berakhot 55b: R. L. said [the checked Bavli has Rabbi Levi] one should await a good dream for twenty-two years, as Joseph’s dreams were fulfilled only after twenty-two years. As Joseph did not reign until twenty-two years after his dream, so the Chaldeans’ words to Rav Yosef were fulfilled only after twenty-two years. Thus the name Yosef caused the same events to occur to each; therefore he resolved that a change of name resembles an act (Berit Shalom, Mikketz). He lived beyond sixty and made a feast for the rabbis because he had passed beyond karet: Moed Katan 28a. When he died the Euphrates’s arches—bridges—kissed one another: Moed Katan 25b. They brought out his bier close to the Shema’s time: Berakhot 19a. For his burial, see Rav Yosef bar Chama.

(7) He sat behind Rabbi Abba, who sat before Rav Huna: Bava Kamma 102a and Avodah Zarah 6b. Abba—another reading Adda; our reading Rav Acha—of Naresh interpreted before him. Abaye was his student; see his entry. He called Abaye and Rava ‘children’: Notel 142b. Rav Adda bar Mattanah was his student; see above. Rav Adda the Elder and Rav Adda bar Ahavah. Rav Avira was in his study house. Rabbi Oshaya said: Eruvin 78a, 88a; Shabbat 127a. Rav Acha be-Rav Yosef thought to say before Rav Yosef; this requires examination. Rav Acha bar Huna transmitted in his name, as did Rav Acha bar Rava. Rav Acha bar Pinchas bar Acha was before him. Idi. Rav Iki bar Rav. Rabbi—it should read Rav—Yosef said: Rabbi Assi said: Rabbi Yochanan said, Shabbat 125b. Rav Bivi. Rav Bivi bar Avin was before him. In Gurin of Asporak’s name. Rav Gaza; see his entry. Rav Dimi bar Yosef was in his study house. He was at Rav Huna’s: end of Mefannin. He sat before Rav Huna: Eruvin 7a. He sat before Rav Huna: Rav Yosef said, Rav Huna told him, and so forth; Rav Yosef turned his face away in anger, Sukkah 11a and Chullin 74a; see Rashi and Tosafot. He sat behind Rav Huna bar Chiyya, who sat before Rav Nachman. Rav Huna bar Minyomi came before him. Rav Huna bar Chinena spoke to him. Rav Huna bar Pinchas transmitted in his name. Huna of Dihemara lived in his time, as did Rabbi Hillel. Bar Vallas asked before him. He sat behind Rabbi Zeira. Mar Zutra be-Rav Nachman was before him. Rav Huna transmitted in his name. Rav Chizkiyah. Rabbi Chiyya said: Ketubbot 87a. Rabbi Chiyya bar Huna. Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin asked him. Rabbi Chama bar Ukva. Rav Chanan bar Tachlifa sent to him. Chanan the tailor taught him a law. Rav Chisda called him ‘master,’ or the reverse; see his entry. Rav Tovyah bar Nechemyah spoke to him. Rabbi Tovi bar Mattanah. Rav Yehudah was his teacher; see above. Rav Yehudah said: Yom HaKippurim 84b. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said. Rav Yosef bar Rava asked him. Rav Yosef bar Menashya’s wife came before him after her husband’s death. Yosef the demon spoke to him: Arvei Pesachim 110a. Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha. He said in Rav Kahana’s name, and sat behind Rav Kahana. Rav Kahana the second was his colleague. Rav Mordekhai asked him. Rabbi Nachman said. Rav Nachman son of Rav Chisda sent to Rav Nachman son of Yaakov [the printed wording is irregular]. Rav Yosef sat before the latter. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak called him Sinai; see above. Natan of Tzutzita lived in his time; see his entry. He flogged Natan the physician. Before Ulla. He drank wine at Mar Ukva’s: Tolin 140a. Anan bar Tachlifa spoke to him. Rabbi Pinchas. Rav said: Yoma 69b, Gittin 38b. He said, ‘From Rabbi’s words we learn’; Rashi explains Rav, Eruvin 11a. Rava was his student; see above. Rava bar Rabbah told him: ‘Let our master teach us.’ Rabbah bar Huna was his colleague. Rabbah called him ‘master’; see above, he was his colleague and asked him. Rabbah bar Ulla. Rabbah bar Shira objected to him. Rabbah son of Rava sent to him. In Rav bar Chana’s name; he asked him. Ravina’s father transmitted in his name. He responds to Ravina the earlier’s words. Rachava came before him. He disputes with Rav Rechumi; this requires examination. Rami bar Abba said. Rami bar Ammi said; this requires examination. Rabbi Shmuel bar Bisna was before him. Rav Shmuel bar Katina told him: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said. Rabbi Shimon Berabbi said. Rav Sheshet was his colleague.
